valuation.method: Forward EPS x P/E: adjusted EPS over the 12 months after the 2027-11 target date (blend of FY2027 and FY2028) times a justified P/E, plus buyback-reduced share count. FY2026 guidance adj. EPS $5.49-5.51; FY2027 revenue guided ~$11.5B (+12%). Model EPS figures are my assumptions, not company guidance.

bear.driver: Narrowbody build-rate and engine-spares slowdown plus gas-turbine order digestion; revenue growth ~6% in 2027, margin gains stall

base.driver: 2027 revenue ~$11.5B (+12%) per guidance, EBITDA margin ~32-33%, $2B FCF funding buybacks (about 1-1.5% share shrink)

bull.driver: Commercial aero and IGT demand exceed guidance, margins rise toward 34%, accelerated buyback under $5.4B authorization

valuation.implied_by_close: At base forward EPS $7.20 the close implies 29.1x; the Yahoo mean target $296 implies 41x at $7.20 or EPS $9.25 at 32x. Close is 38x FY2026 guided EPS $5.50 and about 32x my FY2027 estimate $6.45.
valuation.sensitivity: One turn of P/E moves the base target by $7.20 (3.4 pp of the close)
valuation.watch_metric: Organic revenue growth and adjusted EBITDA margin (Q3 was +25% organic, 32.5% margin) versus the ~12% 2027 revenue growth guide
valuation.next_disclosure: Q4/FY2026 earnings release, expected February 2027 (date not confirmed in sources)

analyst_notes: Only a small named sample could be verified from search snippets (direct fetches of SEC, broker and aggregator pages were blocked), so coverage is partial and no 12-month horizon is documented, so none of these targets enter the weighted target. Named targets ($280-$340) sit 34-63% above the close versus my base of about +10%; at 32x that gap implies EPS of roughly $8.75-$10.60, or a 39-47x multiple on my $7.20. Several targets pre-date the Q3 print and the stock's decline from the ~$265 Q3 buyback price; Yahoo reports a 21-analyst mean of $296 (range $230-$375). Unverified post-Q3 reports of cuts (Morgan Stanley to $300, Jefferies to $350, Susquehanna to $275) were not included for lack of analyst names, dates and primary sources.
